pairs.subject: trust-base
pairs.evidence: scripts/census/run-census.mjs:262 The census is a checker whose verdicts (ratchet baselines) are saved to rules.json and compared on every later --check run. The saved baseline holds only counts and no pin of the engine that produced them, so after a matcher change nobody can tell which baselines a defective engine wrote, and the gate cannot refuse a baseline that a different engine build made.

techniques.evidence: scripts/census/run-census.mjs:262 A stored verdict carries no checker pin. The engine.mjs:304 comparison (`const expected = base[metric];`) acts on that unpinned baseline. A separate per-file sha16 check (PROVENANCE.json, check-library-adherence.mjs:157) does exist, but it hashes files one at a time, fixtures included, rather than the import closure, and it is never attached to a verdict.
scripts/census/lib/engine.mjs:102 The only environment fact in play (CRLF vs LF) is measured at run time. No proof or type-level argument depends on it, so the technique's precondition does not hold.

scripts/census/lib/engine.mjs:27 Plain untyped .mjs on node builtins. There are no escape markers, no re-marked unsafe functions, and no environment writes, so there is no trust-base census to run. (This is a different thing from the repo's 'census' ratchet, which only shares the name.)
scripts/census/lib/engine.mjs:14 No function body is trusted by a prover against a contract. self-test.mjs runs the real engine instead.

pairs.registryProposal: verdict-pins-its-checker reaches well beyond the golden path's prover and type-checker framing. Lint and ratchet gates that store baselines (like this census) fall under it, yet the golden path's use_when never mentions them. Either state that the checker-as-first-member clause covers any stored-verdict gate, or move this technique to quality-gates so seats stop calling these contexts not-applicable.
